html:
SMTO-ART-0023 — SMTO couldn't verify this Task's temporary folders

GUID: b0a92b2e-61c2-482d-b46c-4fe91dcdadc1
Slug: tmp-mapping-invalid
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • Before running a command, the Gateway (the helper program that runs commands on a computer) checks that the Task's private folders belong to this Task. That check failed, so the command didn't start.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the Gateway was recently moved, reinstalled or given a new storage location, ask the person who manages it to finish that change and restart the Gateway. Folders made under the old location no longer match what the Gateway expects.
  2. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to check that its disk has free space and that SMTO's artifacts folder (usually .smto/artifacts in the home folder) can be written. The Gateway must create the Task's folders before any command can start.
  3. Then send the request again in a new message so SMTO starts a fresh Task. The command never started, so sending it again won't repeat anything, and a new Task gets new folders that match it.

What success looks like

  • The command starts and its output appears in the Task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit or delete folders inside the Gateway's artifacts folder by hand; they belong to other Tasks.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway refused to launch because the run's managed workspace could not be validated: required OF_* environment keys were missing, temp, artifact or scratch directories differed from those derived from GATEWAY_ARTIFACT_ROOT, or creating them raised an OS error.

What this means

  • Managed temporary-workspace construction cannot resolve required IDs/directories or rejects their artifact scope/OS validity. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Managed temporary-workspace construction cannot resolve required IDs/directories or rejects their artifact scope/OS validity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect required environment identities and expected managed paths, including the underlying mapping cause.

How to fix it

  • Compare the run's OF_RUN_TEMP_DIR, OF_RUN_ARTIFACT_DIR and OF_RUN_SCRATCH_DIR with the layout derived from the Gateway's GATEWAY_ARTIFACT_ROOT (default ~/.smto/artifacts), and check the Gateway log for the underlying KeyError, ArtifactError or OSError. Restore the original artifact root or start a new run, and fix permissions or disk space on that root.
  • Refresh the owning run's supported workspace mapping without substituting another scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported run workspace produces a coherent verified mapping.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
